reviewed_disposition: known spectroscopic binary; companion mass unresolved
reason: BD-02 2880 = TYC 4885-246-1 = Gaia DR3 3837326955675043456. The 14.7748 d signal has K=16.597 km/s. A SIMBAD SB classification and Gaia NSS flag identify a binary. Missing rotation and stellar mass leave no substellar mass measurement.

Period proximity alone cannot establish a second planet. See the joint model comparison.

reviewed_disposition: unresolved residual in known stellar binary
reason: The 1619.92 d signal was fit with a linear drift. Rickman et al. measured 359.3 ± 10.5 Jupiter masses and a 126 yr orbit for imaged HD 157338 B, including HARPS velocities. Their earlier multi-instrument analysis found no significant residual peak after modeling the binary (thesis Fig. 4.30). The 4.4 yr residual is not the measured binary period, and a distinct companion has not been demonstrated after subtraction of its nonlinear orbit. Rotation is unavailable, the annual fundamental is 6.06 resolution elements away, and there are zero later matched nights.

reviewed_disposition: known planetary system and harmonic overlap
reason: HD 113538 b and c have revised published periods of 663 ± 8 and 1818 ± 25 d from 75 HARPS measurements. This sequential 705.51 d fit is displaced from b and is within 0.76 resolution elements of the third harmonic of the survey's 1929.61 d fit. The other Keplerian projects 5.59 m/s onto the tested frequency. Suárez Mascareño et al. Table A.2 report a 43.9 ± 0.2 d photometric rotation (2.5% FAP). Tuomi et al. Appendix A.32 instead find a 36.38 d photometric period and recover the inner orbit at 655.5 d with HARPS and PFS. Three later ESO nights matched. Evidence for a third body is insufficient.

The 72.4799 d, 1.783 m/s signal passes the internal indicator and offset screens. Target-specific searches using HD 17970, GJ 3187 and HIP 13388 located no matching published planet or secure independent rotation period. Gomes da Silva et al. report low mean chromospheric activity, and Stevenson et al. Fig. B1 document a 2015 line-profile change in this star. Its sampled waveform can correlate at 0.853 with the fifth annual harmonic and 0.998 with the fifth harmonic of the 362.13 d residual. Zero later ESO nights matched. See the same-exposure reduction and season tests for attribution.

The 7.342 d fit matches HD 93385 b at 7.3426 d on the same host.

The 12.455 d velocity period is inside the 12.3–12.5 d rotation range measured in chromospheric lines during one season of epsilon Eridani. The catalog rotation screen missed this time-dependent range. Its low-order annual harmonics are far away, and there are zero later matched nights. The long-period planetary companion is distinct. The rotational explanation prevents a new short-period companion claim.

reason: The 3.873 d fit matches BD-06 1339 b at 3.8728 d on the same host. Lo Curto et al. previously reported this RV period. Simpson et al. later found matching TESS variability and argued for a stellar-activity explanation. NASA flags b as controversial.
